newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares end mixed in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares end mixed in lacklustre trade.

text.p: Stocks across Indian bourses drifted lower on Monday in thin trading volumes and little market action as major participants remained on the sidelines, dealers said.
"The market was stuck in a sideways price movement..a day of subdued trading," said R. Ramakrishnan, chief dealer at ASK-Raymond James Securities India Ltd in Bombay.
"Action is slowly shifting to the broader market."
The BSE's benchmark 30-share index fell 11.69 points or 0.36 percent to close at 3,252.31 after fluctuating in a 50 point trading range.

"The market appears to have bottomed out," ASK's Ramakrishnan said but added that concerns about an impending price hike in petroleum products and an uncertain political situation was likely to put pressure on prices.
Year-on-year Indian inflation, measured by the wholesale price index was at a 56-week high of 7.58 percent on December 21 against 7.08 percent the previous week, the Industry Ministry said on Sunday.
A sharp correction of U.S. stocks by mid-1997 would likely help revive interest in underperforming Asian bourses, said Barton Biggs, Morgan Stanley's chief global strategist.
"...If things work out in Thailand, India and Korea, then those markets could be up 30-35 percent in 1997," he told an investment seminar in Bangkok on Monday.
SBI fell 2.25 rupees to 241.75 and Reliance 0.50 to 216. TISCO rose 0.25 to 181.50 and Bajaj Auto 2.75 to 914.75.
Stocks at the NSE suffered losses on the back of speculative selling by operators, traders said.
A technical problem forced the NSE to suspend trade at 1115 (0545 GMT) hours, NSE officials said. It resumed at 1400 hrs and continued till 1700 hrs, 90 minutes beyond the usual closing time.
